findings.reason: without a liveness or staleness path for a killed in-harness launch, the killed-dispatch case the section's own cases cover for CLI has no counterpart, and the node would land a reservation that can block a run permanently.
findings.text: the constraint "In-harness launches end with their run" frees an in-harness reservation only when its run reaches a terminal phase or its launch is refused, yet a terminal phase is written by a supervisor (dispatch_sessions.py:202) and an in-harness launch starts none (dispatch.py:3037), so an in-harness launch whose dispatching process is killed leaves the run with a held reservation and no path that frees it — the same stranded-reservation defect the section exists to close on the CLI path

findings.reason: a spawn guard that consults no reservation at all passes the spawn-guard case green, so the case as written cannot show the guard fires and the node could land it broken.
findings.text: two of the eight declared cases carry no negative control: the case where a dead launcher with no supervisor and the pointer already at the reserved attempt must be admitted, and the case where the spawn guard must not be refused by its own attempt; the controls index six cases only, and the heading "one case per constraint" understates eight cases for six constraints

response_events.note: §13 now also frees an in-harness reservation when the session its launch was attached to has ended, so a killed in-harness launch strands nothing, with a case.

reasoning-1.note: §13 now also frees an in-harness reservation when the session its launch was attached to has ended, so a killed in-harness launch strands nothing, with a case.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — verified `_retired_attempt_ended` (dispatch_launch.py:2072), `_claim_may_be_reclaimed` (resumption.py:366, current==claimed → False at 381–382), `claim_next_attempt` numbering (resumption.py:398), `LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECONDS` = 120 (recovery_vocabulary.py:55), `_confirm_supervisor_survived` (dispatch_launch.py:2371) with `SUPERVISOR_SURVIVAL_SECONDS` (2313), the in-harness "delegated, not spawned" comment (dispatch.py:3037), `_create_worktree` (dispatch.py:2834) and the `_prepare_attempt_records` call inside the CLI branch (dispatch.py:3438); the new test path is a deliberate creation, not a broken pointer.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §13's done-when declares eight cases under the heading "one case per constraint" but only six carry a logged negative control, leaving the spawn-guard case and the killed-launcher admission case with nothing that shows either can go red.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the reproduction, the armed suite and every negative control are logged under the run directory, with no node-local or scratchpad path named, and each log's header names its revision and command.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test is named for the behaviour it measures and the section's prose carries no plan labels or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the in-harness constraint frees its reservation only when the run reaches a terminal phase or the launch is refused, but nothing writes a terminal phase when the in-harness dispatching process is killed, so that launch holds the reservation forever and contradicts the deliverable's "no launch that has ended, or been killed, leaves the run unlaunchable".
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §13 carries one deliverable (a launch of an existing run id is refused while another launch of it is in flight) and one gate.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — f-arolw-013 now names all four write paths and the section's declared waits (s7→s6, s9→s8, s10→s11) are the only ones whose upstream is still open.
